clue.text: Subvert knowing garden pest

parts.note: vert is the heraldic name for green, and the prefix sub (under) tells us the next piece sits beneath it in this down entry
fly is slang for sharp or knowing

explanation.surface: A sly gardener plots to undermine some cunning pest among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subvert' reads as one verb, but it splits as sub plus vert; vert is heraldry's word for green, which solvers outside heraldry may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly are aphids, small sap-sucking insects that infest roses and other cultivated plants.

clue.text: Old French artist when climbing loses direction

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the painter's name runs backwards
loses tells us one piece is dropped from the turned-round name

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter
S for south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: An elderly French painter loses his bearings while out climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged is an adjective for someone of advanced years, a plain synonym of old.

clue.text: How to deal with Warne's spin?

definitions.text: How to deal with Warne's spin?

indicators.note: spin sends the letters of the word before it turning into a new order

parts.note: the bowler's name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A batsman wonders how to cope with Shane Warne's spin bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: Shane Warne was a famous Australian leg-spin bowler in cricket; the whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman's reply or counter to a bowler is his answer, the response that solves the problem posed.

clue.text: Vehicles Hunt found on board

indicators.note: being found on board a ship means sitting inside it

parts.note: SS is a steamship, and on board means between its letters
Leigh Hunt, the Romantic poet and essayist, gives his first name

explanation.surface: Passengers on a ship search for some kind of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' is not searching but the writer Leigh Hunt, friend of Keats and Shelley.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleighs are sledges drawn over snow by horses or reindeer, so they count as vehicles.

clue.text: Clipper's quicker rounding two points

indicators.note: rounding means going around something, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: faster means quicker
E and N, east and north, two compass points

explanation.surface: A clipper ship is speedier as it rounds a couple of headlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipper' suggests the fast sailing ship, but here it is anything that clips things together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastener such as a paper clip or bulldog clip holds items together, so it clips them.

clue.text: Such a spokesperson can turn a "No", perhaps

parts.note: to spin is to turn
Dr No, the Bond villain, is one example of a doctor

explanation.surface: A slick press officer can turn a flat refusal into good news.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'No' as a refusal; it is really Dr No from the James Bond film, an example of a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a political press adviser who presents events in the most favourable light.

clue.text: Fudge cake made with iron

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to evade an issue with vague talk
second meaning: a crisp batter cake cooked between hinged hot plates

explanation.surface: A recipe for a sweet treat oddly involving iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fudge' looks like the sweet, which suits the baking surface, but it is the verb meaning to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To waffle is to talk evasively, and a waffle is a grid-patterned batter cake made in a waffle iron.

clue.text: Master card

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first version from which copies are made
second meaning: an eccentric, amusing person

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like they belong together as a Mastercard; split them into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An original is the master document copies come from, and also an unusual character, a card in old slang.

clue.text: Turn out a revised paper

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An editor issues a reworked newspaper edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' sounds like producing the paper, but it means to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out for something is to come along and be present, which is to appear.

clue.text: Drop right out of the money

indicators.note: out of here means taken away from, so a letter is removed

parts.note: bread is slang for money
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone drops straight out of the wealthy class.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead is a small round drop of liquid, such as a bead of sweat.

clue.text: Like cancelled debts sent by mail

definitions.meaning: first meaning: debts abandoned as unrecoverable
second meaning: dispatched in a letter

explanation.surface: A creditor posts a note forgiving what someone owes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad debts are formally removed from accounts, and a letter dashed off and posted has been put in writing and sent.

clue.text: Raffia weaving could be cause of marital tangle

indicators.note: weaving interlaces strands, so the letters are woven into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spouse's craft hobby of raffia weaving causes a domestic row.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair, a secret romance outside marriage, is the classic source of trouble between spouses.

clue.text: Square on the high table

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: over the board, board being an old word for table

explanation.surface: A square dish set on the top table at a college dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: High table is where dons dine in an Oxford or Cambridge college hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealings that are honest and open are fair and square, conducted with nothing hidden.

clue.text: Survival from the night before?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a relic or custom left over from an earlier time
second meaning, cryptically: the morning-after misery left by heavy drinking

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how they lived through last night's party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second part as a playful description rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a relic surviving from an earlier time and the morning-after misery from too much alcohol.

clue.text: Routes heading for Yarmouth in area of Norfolk

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Broads are the lakes and waterways of Norfolk, an English county

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the town

explanation.surface: Directions to Great Yarmouth through the Norfolk lake district.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Yarmouth is a Norfolk seaside town, which sells the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Byroads are minor side roads, routes off the main highways.

clue.text: Stakes put on third from last

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means one piece is placed after the other

parts.note: to deposit is to put down

indicators.note: third from asks for the letter in third place of the following word

parts.note: the third letter of the word last

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse to finish third from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third from last' looks like a racing position; read it as the third letter taken from the word last.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes are sums of money put up as bets or pledges, just as deposits are money lodged in advance.

clue.text: They hurl brickbats at the Prince of Wales, perhaps

definitions.text: They hurl brickbats at the Prince of Wales, perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: rioters throwing pieces of brick at royalty
setter's reading: brickbats are harsh remarks, aimed at a public figure

explanation.surface: A mob pelting the heir to the throne with rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Charles was famous for attacking modern architecture, and those who criticised him in turn fit the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics make unfavourable judgements, and a brickbat is a piece of harsh criticism they deliver.

clue.text: Readiness to forgive soldiers in cycle crash

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a crash smashes things, leaving these letters in disorder

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
men is a common word for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are lenient after a bicycle accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Clemency is mercy, the disposition to pardon or treat an offender leniently.

clue.text: It is put in the fire with goose

definitions.text: It is put in the fire

parts.note: and joins things, as with does
a tailor's goose is a heavy smoothing iron

explanation.surface: A goose is roasted over the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goose' points to the bird for roasting, but a tailor's goose is a pressing iron with a goose-neck handle.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal firedog, one of a pair of supports holding logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: "Over-subtle" partly defines punster's wit

indicators.note: partly says only a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A description of a wordsmith's humour as too refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wit' only completes the surface; the letters sit inside the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Finespun means spun very thin, and figuratively too delicate or refined, as of an over-elaborate argument.

clue.text: Ariel's new republic

indicators.note: new implies a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: The spirit from The Tempest founds a new state.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a state in the Middle East with a parliamentary republican constitution, founded in 1948.

clue.text: Trade once common in Europe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: buying and selling, commerce
second meaning: the Common ..., former name of the European community

explanation.surface: Commerce was once a shared European business.
explanation.walkthrough: The Common Market was the popular British name for the European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Market is the sphere of trade, and it completes the phrase Common Market, which Europe once had.

clue.text: Prepare application for a nose job!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put together or get ready
second meaning: cosmetics, as applied when powdering the nose

explanation.surface: Getting the paperwork ready to request cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: A nose job suggests surgery, but it is just powdering the nose with cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up a bed or prescription is to prepare it, and make-up is the cosmetics put on the face.

clue.text: Transport used for getting to Coventry effortlessly?

definitions.text: Transport used for getting to Coventry effortlessly?

parts.note: surface reading: an easy journey to the Midlands city
setter's reading: COVEN plus TRY, a witches' gathering one flies to

explanation.surface: A commuter seeks an easy way to reach Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: Coventry is an English Midlands city; its first five letters spell coven, a meeting of witches.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches traditionally ride through the air on a broom, the long-handled brush used for sweeping.

clue.text: Gun with catches set back

indicators.note: set back means turned to run the opposite way

parts.note: nets catch fish, and to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A firearm whose safety catches have been reset.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: Spotted a number, minus 5

indicators.note: minus means something is subtracted and taken out

parts.note: one number among many
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A number was noticed, less five.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted in the sense of noticed or caught sight of, a past participle like seen.

clue.text: Bishop-in-charge has time for hunting animal

indicators.note: has means the next piece comes along after
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The bishop in charge gets time off to go hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop-in-charge' looks like one title; split it into Bishop, in and charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrets are domesticated polecats used to flush rabbits and rats from burrows.

clue.text: Man in converted coup? shows wealth

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the car, a coupé, whose accented E shows as a question mark in the source
Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man driving a converted sports car displays his riches.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed word was coupé, a two-door car; its accented letter was lost as a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth or luxurious richness.
